what.text: Refugees fleeing Sudan live across host countries in the region, including Chad, South Sudan, Libya, Ethiopia, and Uganda.
By the end of 2025, Libya hosted 551727 refugees from Sudan.
Additionally, 87439 asylum seekers from Sudan were recorded in Libya at the end of 2025.

why.text: The Armed conflict over the government of Sudan was active from 1990 to 2018 with opposition groups SPLM/A, NDA, JEM, SLM/A, NRF, SLM/A - MM, SLFA, SSDM/A, SPLM/A-North, SRF, SSLM/A, Darfur Joint Resistance Forces, and SARC.
The Armed conflict over the government of Sudan continued from 2020 to 2025, involving opposition groups SLM/A, RSF, SPLM/A-North, and SFA.

Other active conflicts recorded include the Armed conflict over Abyei territory, Sudan against Republic of South Sudan in 2011, and the Interstate armed conflict between South Sudan and Sudan against Government of Sudan in 2012.

when.text: Refugee figures for Sudanese in Libya remained lower in earlier years before rising sharply to 199388 at the end of 2024.
By the end of 2025, the year-end refugee figure from Sudan in Libya reached 551727.
This movement occurred during active conflict over the government of Sudan between 2020 and 2025.

how.text: The sources do not detail the travel routes or living conditions of displaced Sudanese people in Libya.
Refugees and asylum seekers are recorded as year-end counts under UNHCR mandate.
Internal displacement metrics for Sudan distinguish between year-end population totals and annual counts of new movements.
